messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>

Subject: Deployment mode & compliance follow-up (HIPAA / SOC 2) - Elara Health

Hi Jordan / Lisa,

Thanks again for the time today - appreciate the overview of Elara's use case and the PHI flows. Quick recap from our discovery so we're aligned and can move to next steps: 

- Scope: clinical note summarization + patient triage routing. Some outputs will be stored in Elara's EHR (PHI).
- Compliance needs: HIPAA (BAA required), SOC 2 Type II report for our security review, and retention of detailed audit logs for 7 years.
- Deployment preference: you asked whether Hosted API could work vs Dedicated capacity or Private VPC/on-prem.

Where Redwood typically lands: for PHI-in-scope production we recommend Dedicated or Private (VPC) because they provide stronger isolation, dedicated GPU pools, and easier auditability. Hosted API can be covered under a BAA for lower-risk integrations, but there are additional controls/contractual requirements (data handling, retention, and region pinning) and we usually validate via a technical review.

Attachments: I'm attaching a short SOC 2 summary and a draft BAA for your legal team to review.

Suggested next steps: 
1) Technical deep-dive with Dylan (solutions engineer) to review network/topology and logging. Can we schedule next week?
2) Legal: review the attached BAA draft - I'll send a DocuSign link once you confirm the contact for redlines.
3) If you prefer Dedicated, we can scope capacity and lead times in the tech call; if you prefer Hosted initially, we can document controls that must be in place under the BAA.

Proposed times for the tech call: Mon 6/21 or Tue 6/22, 10am-1pm PT. Let me know what works.

Best,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa - great summary. A few clarifying questions before we loop legal/infra:

1) SOC 2: do you have the Type II report (last 12 months) and any SOC 2 bridge letter available? Our InfoSec will need to review the full report and control descriptions.
2) Audit logs: we need immutable request-level logs (who/what/when) retained for 7 years and exportable for audits. Can Redwood provide that retention and export format?
3) Deployment mode: our product team prefers Hosted for speed, but our security team is conservative. If Hosted is possible under a BAA, what are the exact limitations (e.g., no RAW PHI persisted in hosted buckets, region pinning, encryption/KMS controls)?

Also: estimated monthly throughput initially ~30M tokens with peak bursts up to 80M. Timeline: procurement/legal approval within 4-6 weeks if the controls check out.

Can we do the tech call on Mon 6/21 10:30am PT?

Subject: Re: Deployment mode & compliance follow-up (HIPAA / SOC 2) - Elara Health

Jordan - great questions. Short answers below and we'll cover details in the call.

1) SOC 2: we can provide the SOC 2 Type II report for the last audit period and a bridge letter. I'll add a secure Drive link before EOD for your InfoSec to access.
2) Audit logs: Redwood provides request-level audit logs (request id, timestamp, model, route, requester, IP, token counts). For Dedicated/Private we support configurable retention and export (JSON/CSV), and for Hosted we can provide exports for up to 1 year by default; 7-year retention is available as an add-on or via Dedicated/Private.
3) Hosted limitations: Hosted can be covered under a BAA for certain integration patterns, but we do NOT recommend storing raw PHI in shared-hosted storage. We require encryption-in-transit + at-rest, region pinning where available, and strict RBAC + tenant separation controls. For high-PHI workloads we recommend Dedicated (reserved capacity) or Private VPC - these give you isolation, customer-managed KMS, and easier audit evidence.

Attachments: SOC2 report summary (same file in case you missed it). I'm also attaching a BAA draft; if you confirm the legal contact I'll route via DocuSign.

Dylan - are you available Mon 6/21 10:30am PT for a 45-minute tech deep-dive on topology and logging?

Thanks,
Marissa
